_README: AI-boundary violation baseline. Read by scripts/check-ai-boundary.mjs.
This is a CEILING, not a target. Each key is `<repo-relative path>::<ruleId>`
and each value is how many occurrences of that rule are KNOWN in that file.
A pair not listed here, or listed with a lower count than reality, FAILS CI.
These 8 entries pre-date the gate being wired into CI (2026-08-31). They are
recorded, not exempted: the rules stay at `error`, and every one of these is a
real violation with a real fix, described in `_entries` below. Fixing one is a
3-step change: fix the code, run `node scripts/check-ai-boundary.mjs --update`,
commit the shrunken baseline in the same PR. `--update` can only SHRINK this
file; adding an entry requires `--accept-new`, which prints a loud warning and
shows up as a reviewable diff hunk here.
Do NOT add an entry to make a red build green. If a violation is genuinely
sanctioned it belongs in docs/architecture/EXCEPTIONS.md with an inline
eslint-disable carrying a `-- see EXCEPTIONS.md E<n>` reason (that is how the
existing /api/tutor/answer exception E5 is handled), not in here.
NOT in this baseline, deliberately: 27 further reports that this config
produced before 2026-08-31 were config bugs, not code violations, and were
fixed at the config layer instead of being baselined. See the two commented
override blocks in .eslintrc.ai-boundary.json for the per-file evidence.

HIGHEST VALUE ENTRY. Line ~323: a select-then-upsert of `concept_mastery`
(mastery_probability / p_know / mastery_level) inside the queue consumer.
This is a SECOND, non-projector canonical writer of the mastery posterior,
which is exactly what ADR-005 forbids, and it is NOT in EXCEPTIONS.md (the
only sanctioned inline mastery write there is E5, /api/tutor/answer).
It also carries a lost-update race: the read and the upsert are separate
round trips, so two concurrent signals for the same (student, topic) can
FIX (owner: ai-engineer + assessment): emit a durable state_events row and
let the concept-mastery projector own the write —
already-allowlisted Deno-side canonical writer with attemptId idempotency.
